gloss: to occur one after another; to happen in succession

definitions.gloss: to occur one after another; to happen in succession; to break out repeatedly
definitions.explanation: For incidents, accidents, or problems to happen one after another in a series. Almost always used for negative events.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}が{続発|ぞくはつ}している。
examples.english: Accidents are happening one after another.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}では{窃盗|せっとう}{事件|じけん}が{続発|ぞくはつ}している。
examples.english: Theft incidents have been occurring one after another in this area.

examples.japanese: {食中毒|しょくちゅうどく}が{続発|ぞくはつ}したため、{保健所|ほけんじょ}が{調査|ちょうさ}に{乗|の}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: After food poisoning cases occurred in succession, the health center launched an investigation.

notes:
Composed of {続|ぞく} (continue, follow) + {発|はつ} (occur, emit). Used almost exclusively for negative events — accidents, crimes, disasters, and problems happening in series.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事故|じこ}が{続発|ぞくはつ}する: accidents occur in succession
- {事件|じけん}が{続発|ぞくはつ}する: incidents happen one after another
- {被害|ひがい}が{続発|ぞくはつ}する: damage occurs repeatedly
- {トラブル}が{続発|ぞくはつ}する: troubles keep arising

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {連発|れんぱつ}する: to occur in rapid succession — can be positive or negative; emphasizes rapid repetition
- {頻発|ひんぱつ}する: to occur frequently — emphasizes high frequency rather than sequential occurrence
- {相次|あいつ}ぐ: to follow one after another — similar meaning and nuance, slightly more literary

REGISTER:
Common in news reports and formal writing. Typically appears in headlines and news stories about crime, accidents, and public health issues.
